pbp_trait_fourth_down_go_rate_reliabilit.classification_evidence: Reliability-only screen (lane J); this entry does not adjudicate a closing ground. Raw within-season Pearson r=+0.3145, 95% season-blocked CI entirely positive [+0.2074,+0.3828], P+=1.0000, Spearman-Brown full-length reliability +0.4785 -- the strongest raw reliability of the four screened metrics. CAVEAT (measured, not a reason to reclassify): unlike the other three metrics (whose label-shuffle nulls sit at +0.0001 to +0.0152), this metric's within-season null centers at +0.2059 (SD 0.0348) and its season-to-season null at +0.3096 (SD 0.0304) -- both far from zero. Because the null only shuffles team labels WITHIN a season, it cannot remove a trend that runs ACROSS seasons, and fourth-down aggressiveness has a well-documented leaguewide increase over 2009-2025; the raw r above is real and positive but likely conflates team-specific persistence with a shared era trend. The excess over the null (~+0.11 within-season, ~+0.10 season-to-season) is the more conservative read of team-specific persistence. Season-to-season replicate (not the recorded effect): r=+0.4124, 95% [+0.2760,+0.5012], P+=1.0000. A real filter bug (play==1 gate silently discarding all punts/FGs, giving a degenerate constant 1.0 go rate) was found and fixed before this measurement; see docs/pbp_trait_reliability.md and the pre-fix artifact kept at artifacts/pbp_trait_reliability/20260905T040022Z/results.json for the record. Earns an ATS look per the task's own bar (non-zero reliability, P+>0.5); ROADMAP LEAD-30 stays open pending the interaction-specific ATS look (BACK aggressive underdogs, FADE aggressive favorites -- never pooled).
